channel.title: Crypto Daybook
channel.description: Crypto Daybook reports daily crypto news: market moves, Bitcoin and Ethereum updates, exchange and protocol developments, regulation and security incidents.

item.title: Why Monero bridge deposits can take longer than expected
item.description: Monero bridge deposits can feel slow when a wallet is still scanning old blocks. Learn how wallet sync, source confirmations and Sepolia delivery affect the wait.

item.title: ZeroFi bridge or swap? Choosing a route for XMR
item.description: A bridge gives XMR an Ethereum token form, while a swap trades it for another coin; choose by where you need the value to end up and what risks you accept.

item.title: Compare Cross-Chain Swap Quotes by What You’ll Receive
item.description: Cross-chain swap quotes estimate what reaches your wallet after fees, price movement, bridge steps and timing, so compare the received amount—not just the rate.

item.title: How to Estimate a Crypto Bridge Transfer Before Sending
item.description: A bridge quote is an estimate, not a promise: compare the source fee, route charge, arrival amount and timing before approving a cross-chain transfer.

item.title: How Polygon PoS checkpoints anchor withdrawals in 2026
item.description: Polygon PoS checkpoints commit Bor block ranges to Ethereum, letting withdrawals prove a burn before tokens can be released on Ethereum mainnet.

item.title: What cross-chain app teams must verify before execution
item.description: Cross-chain app teams should verify a message’s origin, destination and replay status before execution, while accounting for finality and delivery delays.

item.title: Why Cross-Chain Routes Should Rank Reliability Alongside Speed
item.description: For cross-chain swaps, the fastest quote can hide extra steps or thin liquidity; compare expected output, route stages and recovery options before signing.

item.title: Why Destination Liquidity Matters in Cross-Chain Swaps
item.description: Destination-chain liquidity can decide whether a cross-chain swap is usable; integrators should compare delivered amount, token version and fallback routes.

item.title: How to complete a Rango bridge transfer from start to finish
item.description: A Rango transfer combines a source transaction, a cross-chain route and a destination check; compare what leaves and arrives, then track completion on the receiving chain.

item.title: Four Checks for Matching Token Burns to Supply Charts
item.description: A token burn can change reported supply only if the chart tracks the same contract and supply measure; check the transaction, denominator and update timing.

item.title: Trace a New BSC Pair from Its First Blocks
item.description: A new BSC pair can take time to appear in tracking tools. Follow its factory event, liquidity transaction and early swaps to find the pool and assess activity.

item.title: Find where a Mantle bridge transfer is stuck
item.description: A stuck Mantle transfer may be waiting on a source transaction, destination processing or a withdrawal claim. Check each step before sending funds again.

item.title: How batching spreads the cost of crypto withdrawals
item.description: Rollups can prove many withdrawals in one batch, spreading fixed verification costs across users, but each exit still has its own data, claim steps and wait.

item.title: Why Mantle Withdrawals Stay Pending
item.description: Mantle withdrawals can remain pending after initiation because Ethereum must verify the batch, and your wallet may still need to submit a separate claim.

item.title: Check a Bridged Token’s Contract Before You Send
item.description: A token’s ticker does not prove it is the right asset; match its contract to the bridge’s source and destination records before approving a transfer.

item.title: How to Check an Ethereum-to-Manta Transfer
item.description: A successful Ethereum transaction is only the first check: match the bridge deposit, asset, amount and recipient on Manta Pacific before you call it complete.

item.title: Manta bridge fees: what deposits and withdrawals cost
item.description: Manta Bridge costs depend on the network transactions behind each transfer. Learn which side charges gas and what to check before you send funds.

item.title: Set a Swap Limit When an Oracle Check Is Missing
item.description: When a swap has no oracle check, set a minimum output from the live quote, then tighten it for price movement without confusing tolerance with fair value.

item.title: Compare Cross-Chain Swap Fees by What You Receive
item.description: Compare cross-chain swap quotes by the amount that arrives, then check broker, network and liquidity costs, execution risk and quote expiry before you trade.

item.title: Chainflip slippage controls give integrators two price limits
item.description: Chainflip integrators can set a quote-based minimum, an oracle-based price limit and a refund deadline, then use the SDK’s quote recommendations to tune each swap.
